headline: A tiny beginning
momNarrative: You may notice subtle shifts — fatigue, tender breasts, or heightened senses. Rest when your body asks; small routines help.
babyNarrative: The embryo is settling in. The neural tube is forming — the foundation of brain and spinal cord.
gentleTip: Start a prenatal vitamin with folic acid if you have not already.

headline: Heartbeats ahead
momNarrative: Morning sickness or food aversions are common. Eat small, frequent meals and stay hydrated.
babyNarrative: A primitive heart tube is developing. Major organs are beginning to take shape.

headline: Rapid early growth
momNarrative: Hormone surges can affect mood and energy. Be gentle with yourself — this phase is intense but temporary.
babyNarrative: Facial features are starting to form. Arm and leg buds appear as small paddles.

headline: Building foundations
momNarrative: Frequent urination and bloating are normal. Prioritize sleep and light movement if you feel up to it.
babyNarrative: Brain growth accelerates. Tiny hands and feet are becoming more defined.

headline: From embryo to fetus
momNarrative: Nausea may peak around now for many women. Ginger, crackers, and rest can help you through the day.
babyNarrative: Your baby is now officially a fetus. All essential organs have begun to form.

headline: Movement begins internally
momNarrative: Clothes may feel snug as your uterus expands. Maternity bras or looser tops can ease discomfort.
babyNarrative: Muscles are forming. Your baby may make small movements — too early for you to feel.

headline: Critical period complete
momNarrative: Energy may begin to return for some. Continue prenatal care and note questions for your provider.
babyNarrative: Vital organs are in place and continue maturing. Fingers and toes are separating.

headline: Growing quickly
momNarrative: Skin changes or linea nigra may appear. Stay moisturized and use sun protection.
babyNarrative: Head is still large compared to the body. Tooth buds and nasal passages develop.

headline: End of the first trimester
momNarrative: Many women feel relief as nausea eases. You might share news with close family when you are ready.
babyNarrative: Reflexes develop. Vocal cords and fingernails begin to form.
gentleTip: First-trimester screening or nuchal translucency may be discussed at your next visit.

headline: Turning the corner
momNarrative: Appetite often improves. Focus on balanced meals with protein, iron, and fiber.
babyNarrative: Unique fingerprints are forming. Your baby can suck and swallow amniotic fluid.

headline: Second trimester begins
momNarrative: Energy often returns. You may feel more like yourself — a good time for gentle exercise.
babyNarrative: Fine hair called lanugo may cover the skin. The neck lengthens and the head lifts.
gentleTip: Many providers offer anatomy scan planning around mid-pregnancy.

headline: Visible changes
momNarrative: A small bump may show. Round ligament pains — brief sharp sensations — can be normal.
babyNarrative: Bones harden. Your baby can sense light through closed eyelids.

headline: Quickening season
momNarrative: Some mothers feel first flutters now, especially if this is not a first pregnancy.
babyNarrative: The circulatory system is working. Limb movements become more coordinated.

headline: Stronger every day
momNarrative: Backache or nasal congestion can appear. Supportive shoes and pillows help.
babyNarrative: Fat stores begin to develop under the skin. Sweat glands form.

headline: Hearing the world
momNarrative: You might notice dizziness when standing quickly. Rise slowly and stay hydrated.
babyNarrative: Ears stand upright. Your baby hears your heartbeat and voice muffled through fluid.

headline: Protective coating
momNarrative: Skin stretching can itch — moisturize regularly. Stretch marks are common and harmless.
babyNarrative: Vernix caseosa coats the skin. Sensory brain areas specialize for taste and smell.

headline: Halfway there
momNarrative: You may feel clearer kicks now. Sleep on your side when comfortable; pregnancy pillows help.
babyNarrative: Swallowing increases. Meconium accumulates in the intestines.
gentleTip: Anatomy scan often happens near 20 weeks — bring your questions list.

headline: Rhythm and rest
momNarrative: Leg cramps at night are common. Stretch calves and consider magnesium-rich foods if your provider agrees.
babyNarrative: Bone marrow contributes to blood cell production. Movements feel more deliberate.

headline: Features sharpen
momNarrative: Braxton Hicks — practice contractions — may start. They are usually irregular and mild.
babyNarrative: Lips and eyelids are distinct. Taste buds develop on the tongue.

headline: Weight and warmth
momNarrative: You may run warmer than usual. Light layers and cool drinks help.
babyNarrative: Rapid eye movement sleep begins. The skin is still translucent but less so each week.

headline: Viability milestone
momNarrative: Glucose screening for gestational diabetes is often scheduled now. Follow your clinic’s plan.
babyNarrative: Lungs develop surfactant — essential for breathing after birth.

headline: Responsive partner
momNarrative: Heartburn can increase. Smaller meals and avoiding lying down right after eating may help.
babyNarrative: Hands are fully formed. Your baby may respond to familiar voices and music.

headline: Eyes opening
momNarrative: Pelvic pressure may grow. Pelvic floor exercises support comfort now and after birth.
babyNarrative: Eyelids open for the first time. Brain wave activity associated with hearing increases.

headline: Final weeks of trimester two
momNarrative: Restless legs or trouble sleeping are common. A bedtime routine signals your body to wind down.
babyNarrative: Lungs continue maturing. Hiccups — rhythmic taps you may feel — are frequent.

headline: Third trimester begins
momNarrative: Energy may dip again. Pace your days and accept help when offered.
babyNarrative: Fat layers thicken. Your baby can blink and dream during sleep cycles.
gentleTip: Discuss Tdap and any travel or birth-plan topics at upcoming visits.

headline: Busy in there
momNarrative: Shortness of breath can occur as your uterus rises. Sit upright and take breaks on stairs.
babyNarrative: Muscles and lungs keep maturing. Kicks may feel stronger and more visible from outside.

headline: Counting movements
momNarrative: Learn your baby’s typical movement pattern. Report significant changes to your care team.
babyNarrative: Bone marrow takes over more blood production. The brain grows grooves and wrinkles.

headline: Nesting instincts
momNarrative: Frequent bathroom trips return as baby drops lower later — for now, plan breaks on outings.
babyNarrative: All five senses are active. Your baby practices gripping and turning.

headline: Practice for birth
momNarrative: Swelling in feet and ankles can appear late in the day. Elevate legs and stay hydrated.
babyNarrative: Toenails and fingernails reach the tips. The body stores iron and calcium.

headline: Immune transfer begins
momNarrative: Sleep may be fragmented. Side sleeping with support between knees improves comfort.
babyNarrative: Antibodies pass from you to your baby, building early immune protection.

headline: Almost full term
momNarrative: Braxton Hicks may intensify. True labor contractions grow regular, longer, and stronger.
babyNarrative: Lungs near readiness for life outside. Central nervous system matures steadily.

headline: Head down preparations
momNarrative: Pelvic aches and waddling gait are normal. Belly support bands can relieve strain.
babyNarrative: Most babies settle head-down. Kidneys are fully developed; liver processes waste.

headline: Early term approaches
momNarrative: Weekly check-ins often begin. Pack a hospital bag at your own pace — lists help.
babyNarrative: Shedding lanugo and vernix begins. Your baby is gaining about half a pound a week.

headline: Early term
momNarrative: You may feel heavy and eager. Rest, hydration, and gentle walks support the final stretch.
babyNarrative: Lungs and brain continue final tuning. Your baby is considered early term after this week.

headline: Full term
momNarrative: Signs of labor — mucus plug, water breaking, or regular contractions — can start anytime.
babyNarrative: Organs are ready for birth. Your baby practices breathing motions with amniotic fluid.

headline: Any day now
momNarrative: Anxiety and excitement mix — both are normal. Keep your provider’s after-hours number handy.
babyNarrative: The brain continues rapid growth. Fat helps regulate temperature after birth.

headline: Due week
momNarrative: Only about 5% of babies arrive on the due date. Patience and support matter this week.
babyNarrative: Your baby is full term and ready to meet you. Skull bones remain soft for delivery.
gentleTip: If you pass 40 weeks, your care team will discuss monitoring and next steps.
